subject: POC evaluation route and acceptance rubric (decision & next steps)
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Smith <erin.smith@summitcare.com>, Rajesh Nair <rajesh.nair@summitcare.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC evaluation route and acceptance rubric (initial recap)

Thanks again for the call today — great context from the product and ops teams. Quick recap + two suggested paths so we can lock the POC plan and owners. Attachment: POC-Success-Criteria-v1.xlsx and shadow-eval-rubric.pdf.

Summary of ask/discovery:
- Goal: validate automated triage accuracy for clinical routing (trigger -> correct destination) at production latency (<300ms median) and acceptable false-positive rate for clinician escalation.
- Expected labeled sample: ~5k anonymized transcripts from last 90 days (we discussed scope).
- Data constraints: PHI-aware workflow, SummitCare wants KMS audited retention and strict audit logs.

Two recommended evaluation routes (pros/cons):
1) Offline batch evaluation (fast iteration)
   - Redwood runs model against a labelled holdout set, returns per-case grade and aggregate metrics (precision/recall, latency distribution).
   - Pros: lowest risk for PHI, rapid iterations, clear pass/fail gates.
   - Cons: may miss live distribution drift and system integration edge-cases.
2) Online shadow (live, non-blocking)
   - Model runs in parallel to prod routing, outputs are logged and scored vs. eventual human action; no live decisions made during shadow.
   - Pros: captures real traffic distribution and latency under load.
   - Cons: extra operational controls for PHI, needs KMS+audit enabled and a short retention policy for shadow logs.

Proposed acceptance gates (we put more detail in the attached spreadsheet):
- Primary quality gate: >= 92% correct routing on holdout OR shadow F1 >= 0.88 with false-positive rate <= 4%.
- Latency gate: median end-to-end inference + routing < 300ms, 95th < 600ms.
- Reliability gate: <1% inference error rate and successful KV cache hit improvements across session-length distributions.

Ownership & timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (kickoff): legal + security checklist, KMS+audit configuration (SummitCare + Redwood infra). Owner: Rajesh (SummitCare) + Karthik (Redwood SRE).
- Weeks 1–2: Offline evaluation run against labeled set (if you prefer quick turn). Owner: Marissa (Redwood PM) + SummitCare labeling team.
- Week 3: Optional 1-week shadow run to validate live behavior; can be run in parallel with remediation plan. Owner: Karthik (Redwood) + Rajesh (SummitCare).

Decision requested: would you prefer we start with the offline run (fast path) or go straight to a short shadow run (higher fidelity)?

Next steps I propose:
- Please confirm preferred route by EOD Thu (7/1).
- If offline: share the label sample and we’ll return first report within 10 business days.
- If shadow: confirm retention window and any additional masking requirements; we’ll provision a shadow endpoint with short retention and audit logging.

Thanks — happy to jump on 20m to talk through.

—
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Erin Smith <erin.smith@summitcare.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajesh Nair <rajesh.nair@summitcare.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC evaluation route and acceptance rubric (initial recap)

Thanks Aisha — useful summary. A few clarifying points from our side before we lock route:

1) PHI/data handling: our security team will only approve shadowing if we can audit KMS keys and enforce a 7-day retention for logs; is that feasible?
2) Label set: we can provide a 5k de-identified sample but will need instructions on the exact formatting and hashing scheme for IDs.
3) SLA: in a shadow run we want clear signals for when Redwood would flip to fallback (e.g., if error rate spikes) — can you surface the health check thresholds?

Preference: leaning toward starting with the offline run to get baseline metrics, then progress to a short shadow to validate live behaviour. That gives our security team time to validate KMS configuration.

Can Rajesh (copied) confirm who on our side will own the label handoff?

Erin
Head of Product Operations, SummitCare
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Smith <erin.smith@summitcare.com>, Rajesh Nair <rajesh.nair@summitcare.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC evaluation route and acceptance rubric (initial recap)

Hi Erin / Rajesh —

Short answers up front: 7-day retention + KMS audit is supported; we’ll provide the KMS key fingerprint and the audit log export. Health thresholds we use for automated fallback are configurable, we can start with conservative defaults and expose them in the console.

A few notes on eval methodology and the grading rubric (high level):
- Offline grading: we compute per-case labels and aggregate confusion matrices, report precision, recall, F1, and headroom by intent bucket. We also produce latency histograms by request token count so you can see model cost tradeoffs.
- Shadow grading: we capture model outputs and a lightweight provenance envelope (request id, model version, inference latency, cache_hit). We compare to eventual human routing; where human routing is delayed we mark as pending.

Suggested pragmatic path (minimize ops friction):
1) Week 1–2: Offline run on your 5k de-id sample. Deliverable: offline report, per-intent breakdown, and recommended model/config (quantization + batching) for shadow stage.
2) Week 3: Shadow for 5 business days at 10% traffic, retention 7 days, with KMS audit enabled. If shadow shows F1 >= 0.88 and false-positive <= 4%, we pass quality gate. If offline already meets quality gate we can optionally shorten shadow to 2–3 days focused on tail behavior.

Rubric (short):
- Per-case score: 1 = correct routing, 0 = incorrect routing, NA = insufficient ground truth.
- Aggregation: F1 (primary), precision (for escalation sensitivity), latency percentiles (median, 95th).
- Pass condition: (Offline F1 >= 0.92) OR (Shadow F1 >= 0.88 AND FP <= 4%) AND latency gates met.

Ownership:
- Label handoff format: CSV with columns {anon_id, timestamp, transcript, gold_route}. Rajesh / SummitCare to own.
- Redwood will own infra provisioning, endpoint creation, and report generation. Marissa will be PM for deliverables and timelines.

I’ve pulled the more detailed rubric into the attached PDF and updated the spreadsheet with the timeline. HubSpot link and Drive doc are in my signature.

Karthik
Director, SRE — Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks for the alignment everyone. Agreed path: start with the offline run (Week 1–2) then a short 5-business-day shadow at 10% (Week 3) assuming security sign-off on KMS. Action items:

- Rajesh / SummitCare: share the 5k de-id csv (format guidance in attached spreadsheet) by EOD Mon 7/5.
- Karthik / Redwood: provision offline runner and share initial config; set up KMS audit exports in parallel.
- Marissa / Redwood: create a one-pager for the internal kickoff and schedule a 30m kickoff for Wed 7/7 — calendar link in related_links.

I’ll draft a short mutual action plan and share a signed scope that we can attach to HubSpot after kickoff.

If that works I’ll send a calendar invite for Wed 7/7 10:00am PT.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

—
Aisha
